idiom_name: type constructor + pure/unit + bind, interpreted at the edge
implementation_notes: Language-neutral recipe: represent the effect as a type constructor M with two operations - pure/unit : a -> M a and bind : M a -> (a -> M b) -> M b - so every step is a total function into M and the propagation rule (absence, failure, asynchrony, state) lives inside bind. Derive map from bind, keep the effect primitives (fail, await, get/put, putStrLn) next to the instance, and run the pipeline through one interpreter at the program boundary. Check the three laws (left identity, right identity, associativity) with property tests before publishing a custom instance: a bind that breaks associativity silently changes behaviour when call sites are refactored or when the compiler desugars sugar into bind.
code_sketch:
-- M a : a computation over a that also carries effect E
pure  :: a -> M a                     -- unit: no effect
(>>=) :: M a -> (a -> M b) -> M b     -- bind: propagate E, continue with the value

pipeline :: M C
pipeline = step1 >>= (\x -> step2 x >>= (\y -> pure (combine x y)))

run pipeline                          -- effect-specific interpreter at the edge
pitfalls: Writing bind without the laws: an eager or non-associative bind changes behaviour under refactoring and compiler desugaring.
Using bind where map suffices, inventing a dependency on the previous value that the step does not have.
Leaking the effect into step bodies: unwrapping mid-pipeline or catching what the monad is supposed to propagate.
Wrong move: use bind or and_then when the next operation is a pure value transformation -> the extra effectful layer obscures intent and can change the computation shape -> instead use map.

Wrong move: start independent asynchronous effects with sequential thenCompose -> the pipeline waits for each dependency and sacrifices available parallelism -> instead combine independent stages with an applicative or parallel operation such as Promise.all or Task.WhenAll.

Wrong move: unwrap or run the monad in the middle of a pipeline -> failures and effect policy escape into ad-hoc control flow and become hard to compose -> instead keep M a through the steps and interpret once at the program edge.
